messages:
maria: Heads-up: us-west-2a saw ECC spikes on pool-gpu-7 around 05:30 UTC. Short burst pattern across 4 cards, correctables high but no Xid 13 yet. Observed tail latency bumps on a few routes.
jonathan: Seen it, digging. Are these per-card bursts or rack-level? I see card_id 87 and 90 repeated in the metrics.
sasha: Posting quick telemetry query we can run: ```sql
SELECT card_id, count(*) AS c FROM ecc_events WHERE region='us-west-2a' AND ts > now() - interval '15 minutes' GROUP BY card_id ORDER BY c DESC;
```
infra-bot: Alert: ECC burst detected in us-west-2a. 4 cards exceed 30/hr threshold. Incident ID: ECC-2026-2334.
ashwin: We should avoid immediate hard-drain. Proposal: graded suppression -> if burst < 2m ignore; if 2-30m then soft-drain (stop scheduling new work, migrate new pods); if >30m then mark for replace. Thoughts?
lena: Cost note: soft-drain causes job requeues and preemptible costs spike; we need a gate by job-failure/oom/Xid correlation. Do we have a cheap way to correlate with job failures?
maria: Yes. Quick manual check: `grep "Xid 13" /var/log/gpu-*/events.log` plus allocator OOMs. Operationally I propose auto-drain only when ECC >= 60 in 30m OR any Xid is present AND app error rate delta > 0.2%.
jonathan: Could we instead add noise suppression: require sustained rate and a cluster-level degradation signal (e.g., p99 latency up >10%)? That will avoid draining noisy cards that don't impact customers.
sasha: We can implement it in the detection pipeline: moving-window filter + exponential backoff for drain signals. Pseudocode: ```py
if ecc_rate(card, 30m) > threshold and cluster_p99_increase > 0.1:
    trigger_soft_drain(card)
else:
    suppress_until(window * 2)
```
ashwin: Ops playbook updates (draft): 1) Run `gpu-health scan --card 87` to collect hw logs. 2) If soft-drain triggers, set `soft_drain_ttl=2h` and move pods with `evict --grace=60s --live_migrate=true`. 3) If Xid seen or repeat within 72h, open replace ticket and tag `hw-warranty`.
maria: :thumbsup: Add to runbook but also we need a temporary reduction in auto-drain sensitivity for us-west-2a due to low spare capacity this week. Recommend raising threshold from 30 -> 50 for this zone until capacity replenishes, with strict rollback if customer impact detected.
lena: Agree on raising threshold but require manual override to force drain if customer-impact detected. Also add billing-owner alert when requeues exceed baseline.
jonathan: I'll add a flamegraph and a short memory-saturation test to detect ECC-driven memory scrubbing. Also want to enrich telemetry with driver/kernel version, pci_slot and BIOS to help HW correlation.
infra-bot: Action created: ECS-1221 - Update auto-drain policy for region us-west-2a (assignee: jonathan).
sasha: I'll draft the PR for suppression logic and add unit tests. Recommend a 48h canary on us-west-2a with extra alerting.
maria: Canary + alerting rule: create alert that fires if suppressed drains > 3 in 6h. If so, revert suppression immediately and escalate.
ashwin: Also note: when soft-draining, prefer live-migrate long-running jobs instead of restart to save costs. Add `live_migrate=true` flag to evict tool and document expected requeue cost.
lena: I'll update the cost dashboard to show estimated requeue costs per evict so PMs and finance can see tradeoffs.
jonathan: Will push PR this afternoon and tag @sasha for review. Uploading telemetry bundle to S3: s3://redwood-ecc-telemetry/us-west-2a/2223334444/
maria: :white_check_mark: Closing loop — temporary suppression + canary plan + ops playbook steps + replace ticket path if repeats. Keep updates here and paste CI run results when PR lands.
